collection.description: A planter offers young noni plants for food for the journey home.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A soft-spoken planter named Malu arrives with a canoe full of young noni plants, their roots wrapped in wet moss. He says the village's bushes would bear far more if he set his young plants among them, and he asks for food for the journey home. (name1) has to decide.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) helps Malu plant every one. Within a season, the noni bushes around the village are heavy with fruit.

o3.name: Outcome C
o3.text: (name1) explains the village cannot spare food just now. Malu leaves one small plant by the path anyway, "to remember him by."

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Haggle, the better deal
o2.text: (name1) offers to carry water to the new plants for Malu. He is so grateful that he plants his last bundle too, the ones he was saving for his own garden.

o2b.name: Haggle, the worse deal
o2b.text: (name1) haggles, and Malu, who is tired, plants only half and leaves the rest in the canoe.

nothing.name: Nothing to trade
nothing.text: Malu sees the village has little food to spare and leaves one small plant by the path as a gift.
